notes: Awaran was a sub-division of Khuzdar district until it was notified as a separate district on 11 November 1992 (BHC says November 1992; Wikipedia cites the 1998 DCR of Awaran p.1 and the UN/Balochistan Bureau of Statistics profile for the exact date); before 1974 the area was inside Kalat district and before 1955 inside Kalat State.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - About Session Court Awaran; corroborated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awaran_District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Awaran)

notes: Barkhan was a tehsil of Loralai district until it was granted separate district status on 31 December 1991 when Loralai was split into Loralai, Barkhan and Musakhel (BHC and the 1998 DCR of Barkhan p.1 as cited by Wikipedia agree).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Barkhan; corroborated by Wikipedia Barkhan District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Barkhan)

former_names: Kachhi District (1965-1991); renamed Bolan 31 December 1991; renamed Kachhi again in 2008
notes: The Kachhi plain was part of Kalat State (1951) and then Kalat district; Kachhi was notified as a district in February 1965 (Wikipedia, uncited; the Kalat District page agrees on 1965), lost Nasirabad in 1974 and Jhal Magsi in December 1991, at which point the remainder was renamed Bolan (1998 DCR of Jhal Magsi p.1 as cited by Wikipedia), and Bolan was renamed Kachhi in April 2008 (Daily Times).
source_title: Wikipedia - Kachhi District (1965 notification uncited; 2008 renaming cites Daily Times 28 Apr 2008); BHC Jhal Magsi history page for the 1991 renaming

notes: Chagai was one of the British Baluchistan districts (administration taken over from the Khan of Kalat in 1896, HQ then at Nushki) and has existed continuously; Nushki was separated from it after the 1998 census (reported 2004) and Taftan in 2026.
source_title: Wikipedia - Chagai District (infobox Established 1896, uncited); FIBIS wiki Baluchistan Districts lists Chagai (HQ Nushki) among British Baluchistan districts

notes: The Bugti tribal area (Marri-Bugti Country) was administered within Sibi district until Dera Bugti was established as a separate district in July 1983 (1998 DCR of Dera Bugti p.13 as cited by Wikipedia; BHC Sibi history page also gives 1983).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Sibi; corroborated by Wikipedia Dera Bugti District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Dera Bugti, July 1983)

notes: Gwadar was a tehsil of Makran district (the former Makran State; Gwadar town itself was Omani until 1958) until Makran district was trifurcated into Turbat (now Kech), Panjgur and Gwadar districts on 1 July 1977 when Makran Division was formed; the parent is listed as Kech because Kech is the 1998 successor of Makran district.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Panjgur (Makran district split 1 July 1977); corroborated by Wikipedia Gwadar District (Established 1 July 1977)

notes: Jafarabad was created in 1987 by bifurcating Nasirabad district (the rest of Nasirabad was briefly called Tamboo district, July 1987 to December 1990), per the 1998 DCR of Nasirabad p.13 and Pakistan Almanac as cited by Wikipedia; the month is inferred from the Tamboo renaming date and is not separately confirmed.
source_title: Wikipedia - Jafarabad District (cites Pakistan Almanac); Wikipedia Nasirabad District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Nasirabad p.13)

notes: Jhal Magsi was part of Kachhi district until December 1991 when it was made a district under the name Kachhi while the remainder of old Kachhi was renamed Bolan; the new district was renamed Jhal Magsi in May 1992 (BHC and the 1998 DCR of Jhal Magsi p.1 as cited by Wikipedia agree).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Jhal Magsi (Gandawa); corroborated by Wikipedia Jhal Magsi District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Jhal Magsi)

notes: Kalat was a princely state at the 1951 census (the 1951 figure covers the whole state including the later Khuzdar, Mastung, Kachhi, Jhal Magsi and Awaran areas) and was made a district on 3 February 1954 (1998 DCR of Nasirabad p.13 as cited by Wikipedia; Kalat District page gives the same date), then lost Kachhi (1965), Khuzdar (1974), Mastung (1991) and later Surab (2017).
source_title: Wikipedia - Kalat District (3 February 1954, uncited); corroborated by Wikipedia Nasirabad District citing 1998 District Census Report of Nasirabad p.13

former_names: Makran State (to 1955); Makran District (1955-1977); Turbat District (1977-1994/95); renamed Kech 1994-95
notes: Makran State became Makran district of Kalat Division on 14 October 1955 and on 1 July 1977 Makran district was split into Turbat, Panjgur and Gwadar districts (BHC Panjgur page); Turbat district was renamed Kech in 1994-95 (Balochistan Police as cited by Wikipedia); Kech is treated as the residual successor of Makran district, so no 1998 parent is listed; the 1951 and 1961 figures refer to the Kech/Turbat part of Makran State/district.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Panjgur (Makran district split 1 July 1977); Wikipedia Kech District (renaming 1994-95, cites Balochistan Police); Wikipedia Makran Division (Makran district 14 Oct 1955)

notes: Kharan was a princely state at the 1951 census and became a district of Kalat Division when the Balochistan States Union was dissolved on 14 October 1955 (Wikipedia Kalat Division lists Kharan among the four original districts); the BHC page instead says the former state territory was organized as Kharan district in 1970, so the exact date is disputed; Washuk was split from it in 2005/2007.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Kharan; Wikipedia Kalat Division (1955 four districts: Kalat, Makran, Lasbela, Kharan)

notes: Khuzdar was part of Kalat district (and before that Kalat State) until it was established as a separate district by notification of 1 March 1974 (BHC and Wikipedia agree); Awaran was split from it in November 1992.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Khuzdar; corroborated by Wikipedia Khuzdar District and Kalat District (1 March 1974)

notes: Killa Abdullah was separated from Pishin district and made a new district in June 1993 (BHC; the 1998 DCR of Pishin p.1 as cited by Wikipedia gives 1993); before 1975 the area was in Quetta-Pishin district.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Killa Abdullah; corroborated by Wikipedia Pishin District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Pishin)

notes: Killa Saifullah was established as a district in 1988 from two former administrative units of Zhob district, the Upper Zhob sub-division and the sub-tehsil of Badinai (BHC and the 1998 DCR of Killa Saifullah pp.1,8 as cited by Wikipedia agree); no month found.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Killa Saifullah; corroborated by Wikipedia Killa Saifullah District (cites 1998 District Census Report)

notes: The Marri tribal area was administered within Sibi district until Kohlu was created as a district in 1974 when Sibi was subdivided to create Nasirabad and Kohlu (BHC Sibi history page; Wikipedia infobox also gives 1974); no exact date found.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Sibi; corroborated by Wikipedia Kohlu District (Established 1974, uncited)

notes: Las Bela was a princely state at the 1951 census and became a separate district on 30 June 1954 (BHC; Wikipedia infobox June 1954); it was attached to Karachi-Bela Division from 1960 to 1972 and then returned to Kalat Division, and Hub was split from it in 2022.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Lasbela (Hub); corroborated by Wikipedia Lasbela District (Established June 1954)

notes: Loralai was created as a British Baluchistan district in October 1903 by remodelling the Thal Chotiali and Zhob agencies and has existed continuously; Barkhan (31 December 1991) and Musakhel (1 January 1992) were carved from it, and Duki later in 2016.
source_title: Government of Balochistan - History of District Loralai; Balochistan High Court Musakhel history page (Loralai divided into three districts)

notes: Mastung was a sub-division of Kalat district until it was granted district status in July 1991 and began functioning independently on 18 February 1992 (SMEDA district profile as cited by Wikipedia; BHC gives 1991; the Wikipedia districts list gives December 1991), so the year is secure but the month is disputed.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Mastung; corroborated by Wikipedia Mastung District (cites SMEDA District Economic Profile Mastung 2022, p.26)

notes: Musakhel was a tehsil of Loralai district until it was notified as a district on 1 January 1992 when Loralai was split into Loralai, Barkhan and Musakhel (BHC and the 1998 DCR of Musakhel p.1 as cited by Wikipedia agree; the Wikipedia districts list's 11 November 1992 is an outlier).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Musakhel; corroborated by Wikipedia Musakhel District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Musakhel)

notes: Nasirabad was notified as a district in 1974 (BHC; 1998 DCR of Nasirabad p.13 as cited by Wikipedia), but sources disagree on the parent: the BHC Sibi page says Sibi was subdivided in 1974 to create Nasirabad and Kohlu, the DCR says it was separated from Kalat, and the Kachhi and Kalat Wikipedia pages say Nasirabad was inside Kachhi district (Kalat Division) from 1965, so the 1998 Nasirabad area was in Sibi district in 1951 and 1961 (Nasirabad tehsil) and most likely in Kachhi (Bolan) at the 1972 census; Jafarabad was split from it in 1987 and the remainder was called Tamboo district until December 1990.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Nasirabad (Dera Murad Jamali); Wikipedia Nasirabad District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Nasirabad p.13); BHC Sibi history page

notes: Nushki was NOT a district at the 1998 census (Balochistan then had 26 districts and Nushki was a sub-division of Chagai, where the colonial district HQ had been); it was separated from Chagai in 2004 according to the Wikipedia districts list (uncited) and Dawn of 22 May 2005 already counts 27 districts, so the 1998 figures printed for it are a later PCO restatement.
source_title: Wikipedia - List of districts in Balochistan (Nushki separated from Chagai 2004, uncited; 26 districts at 1998 census); Dawn 22 May 2005 'Kharan split into 2 districts' (27 districts before the split)

notes: Panjgur was one of the three tehsils of Makran district (formerly Makran State) until 1 July 1977 when Makran Division was formed and Panjgur, Turbat (Kech) and Gwadar became districts; the parent is listed as Kech because Kech is the 1998 successor of Makran district.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Panjgur; corroborated by Wikipedia Panjgur District (1 July 1977)

notes: Pishin was part of the British-era Quetta-Pishin district until 1975 when Quetta and Pishin were made separate districts (BHC; 1998 DCR of Pishin p.1 as cited by Wikipedia); Killa Abdullah was split from it in June 1993.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Pishin; corroborated by Wikipedia Pishin District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Pishin)

notes: Quetta, Pishin and Shorarud were formed into one administrative charge in 1883 and the unit was known as Quetta-Pishin district through the 1951, 1961 and 1972 censuses; in 1975 it was bifurcated into Quetta and Pishin districts, so the 1998 Quetta district is the residual of Quetta-Pishin (the 1951 figure in the input covers the whole Quetta-Pishin district).
source_title: Wikipedia - Quetta District (cites Imperial Gazetteer of India v.21 and Balochistan High Court History of District); BHC Pishin history page (1975 separation)

notes: Sibi was established as a British Baluchistan district in 1903 (then including the Marri-Bugti country and Nasirabad tehsil) and has existed continuously; it lost Nasirabad and Kohlu in 1974, Dera Bugti in 1983, Ziarat in 1986 and later Harnai (2007) and Lehri (2013-2018).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Sibi; corroborated by Wikipedia Sibi Division (Sibi district created 1903)

former_names: Fort Sandeman (headquarters name until 30 July 1976; district sometimes so called)
notes: Zhob was formed as a British Baluchistan district (agency) in 1890 with Fort Sandeman as headquarters, renamed Zhob town on 30 July 1976, and has existed continuously; Killa Saifullah was carved from it in 1988 and Sherani in 2006.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Zhob; corroborated by FIBIS wiki Baluchistan Districts (Zhob, HQ Fort Sandeman)

notes: Ziarat was part of Sibi district until it was established as a separate district in July 1986 (1998 DCR of Ziarat p.13 as cited by Wikipedia; BHC Sibi history page also gives 1986).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Sibi; corroborated by Wikipedia Ziarat District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Ziarat, July 1986)

notes: Quetta-Pishin was the British Baluchistan district covering the 1998 Quetta, Pishin and Killa Abdullah districts; it was bifurcated into Quetta and Pishin in 1975, so it existed at the 1951, 1961 and 1972 censuses but not in 1981.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Pishin; Wikipedia Quetta District (Imperial Gazetteer of India v.21)

notes: Makran State was enumerated as a state in 1951, became Makran district of Kalat Division on 14 October 1955 (with Gwadar added as a tehsil in 1958), and was split into Turbat (Kech), Panjgur and Gwadar districts on 1 July 1977 when Makran Division was formed; the Wikipedia Makran Division page dates the split to 1 July 1970, which conflicts with the BHC Panjgur page and the Gwadar and Panjgur district pages (1977).
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Panjgur; Wikipedia Makran Division (Makran district 14 Oct 1955)

notes: Kachhi district (Kalat Division) was notified in February 1965 out of Kalat district and at the 1972 census covered the 1998 Bolan, Jhal Magsi and (per Wikipedia) Nasirabad and Jafarabad areas; Nasirabad left in 1974 and when Jhal Magsi was separated on 31 December 1991 the remainder was renamed Bolan, which is the 1998 unit, so this row is the same territory as BOLAN DISTRICT before 1991.
source_title: Wikipedia - Kachhi District (February 1965 notification, uncited); Wikipedia Kalat District (Kachhi separated 1965); BHC Jhal Magsi history page

notes: Tamboo district is only a temporary name (July 1987 to December 1990) for the Nasirabad district remainder after Jafarabad was split off in 1987, so it is the same unit as NASIRABAD DISTRICT and did not exist at any census date.
source_title: Balochistan High Court - History of District Nasirabad (Dera Murad Jamali); Wikipedia Nasirabad District (cites 1998 District Census Report of Nasirabad p.13)

notes: The Bolan Pass (Bolan Agency) is listed among the six British Baluchistan districts from 1911 (Wikipedia districts list; FIBIS wiki), but no source was found stating whether it was still a separate district at the 1951 census or when and into which district it was merged, so its 1951 status is not found.
source_title: FIBIS wiki - Baluchistan Districts (lists Bolan Pass, HQ Kalat); Wikipedia List of districts in Balochistan (1911 six districts incl. Bolan)
